period_note: Year-end (31 December 2025) position from NRB Commercial Bank's 'Annual Integrated Report 2025', taken from its own 'Five Years' Key Performance Indicators' table (printed pages 49-50, physical PDF pages 50-51), which is explicitly captioned 'Last Five years' (2021 to 2025) Balance Sheet (Solo)' / '...Profit & Loss Statement (Solo)' elsewhere in the same report. Basis is therefore explicitly SOLO, confirmed both by that caption and by the standard match-total-assets method: this table's own FY2024 column for 'Size of Balance Sheet' (230,593.06) reproduces the existing dataset's stored solo FY2024 total_assets exactly. This PDF is entirely image-based (pdftotext -layout returns 0 lines; native embedded page images are only 845x1233px at 72ppi) so all figures were read directly off the rendered table image at 300dpi with additional 2-3x crops/zooms on ambiguous cells, and cross-checked line-by-line against the existing FY2024 record for consistency (see discrepancies below). DISCREPANCIES FOUND vs the already-stored FY2024 record (FY2024 file left unchanged; both values recorded here): (1) Deposit: FY2024's own report states 183,282.14; this FY2025 report's FY2024 comparative column states 169,737.39 instead (a 13,544.75 / 7.4% reduction). Total assets (230,593.06) and gross loans (147,576.45) for FY2024 reproduce exactly across both reports, so this looks like a reclassification within liabilities (some deposit-like balance moved to another liability line) rather than a broad restatement. (2) Profit after tax: FY2024's own report states 35.88, which does not arithmetically reconcile with that same report's own profit-before-tax (44.43) minus provision for taxation (-0.34) = 44.77. This FY2025 report's FY2024 comparative column states 44.77, which DOES reconcile exactly with the same PBT/tax figures (both reports agree PBT=44.43 and tax=-0.34). This mirrors the ISLAMIBANK FY2024-capital precedent: the contemporaneous figure is arithmetically inconsistent with its own report, while the later report's comparative is internally consistent. (3) 'Operating income' definitional difference (not a value restatement): FY2024's own report's five-year table computed 'Operating income' as gross interest income + investment income + non-interest income = 12,481.25+5,548.54+1,772.77 = 19,802.56 (before deducting interest expense). This FY2025 report's table computes the same line as NET interest income + investment income + non-interest income = 187.02+5,548.54+1,772.77 = 7,508.33 for the identical FY2024 year. Every underlying component (interest income, interest expense, net interest income, investment income, non-interest income) reproduces exactly across both reports, so this is purely a change in which formula the bank's own report labels 'Operating income', not a restated transaction; total_operating_income below uses THIS report's own (net-interest-income-based) figure for FY2025, consistent with how FY2025's own table defines it. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY found within the FY2025 report's own table (not a cross-report issue): Core Capital/Tier I (11,481.23) + Supplementary Capital/Tier II (7,389.06) = 18,870.29, but the same table's own 'Regulatory Capital [Tier I + II]' row prints 18,083.74 (786.55 / 4.3% short of the sum of its own two components). Three independent figures in the same table tie out to 18,083.74 and not to 18,870.29: Capital Surplus/(Shortfall) of -2,183.36 equals 18,083.74 minus Capital Requirement of 20,267.10 exactly; CRAR of 11.15% equals 18,083.74 / RWA of 162,136.81 exactly; and the printed Tier-II Capital Ratio of 4.07% implies a Tier II capital of approximately 6,599-6,603 (RWA x 4.07%, and also exactly 18,083.74 minus the printed Tier I of 11,481.23 = 6,602.51), not the printed 7,389.06. The Tier-I ratio (7.08%) does tie to the printed Tier I capital. All three re-verified visually at 3x crop zoom - the printed digits are unambiguous. This strongly suggests the printed Tier II CAPITAL AMOUNT cell (7,389.06) is a typo in the source document; it is recorded here exactly as printed (basis 'reported'), with total_capital taken as the table's own printed total (18,083.74, consistent with its CRAR and capital-surplus rows) rather than derived by summing the two tier components as prior years' methodology would otherwise do. Asset-quality and capital trends continued to deteriorate in FY2025 despite a profit recovery: NPL rose to 17.17% (from 15.47%), CRAR fell to 11.15% (from 12.00%) and the capital shortfall widened to -2,183.36 (from -754.81); Tier-1 fell to 7.08% (from 7.64%). Profit after tax recovered to 329.83m from the FY2024 trough (35.88m per FY2024's own report / 44.77m per this report) but remains far below FY2021-2023 levels (1,739.57-2,083.94m). ldr_pct below uses the bank's own reported 'Credit Deposit Ratio' (77.71%), which does not equal a naive gross-loans/deposits calculation from this same table (162,469.79/198,424.61=81.88%) - likely a regulatory definition or averaging difference; both figures are noted here for transparency.
